tournament: FIFA World Cup 26 — United States · Canada · Mexico

quickFacts.text: Golden Boot: three-way tie on 7 goals

hero.headline: GIANTS FALL IN NEW JERSEY
hero.standfirst: Erling Haaland struck twice in the last eleven minutes to send Brazil home and carry Norway into a World Cup quarter-final for the first time in the nation's history — on the very pitch where the final will be played two weeks from now.
hero.photoCaption: Erling Haaland — two goals in eleven minutes, seven for the tournament

briefing.text: FIFA reversed Folarin Balogun's red-card suspension on review — the striker can face Belgium tonight.
England sweat on two: Quansah is suspended for the quarter-final, and Jordan Henderson hurt an arm in the post-match celebrations.
Last two round-of-16 ties tomorrow, rest day Wednesday — then the quarter-finals begin Thursday in Boston.

facts.text: Brazil's 34% possession — their lowest ever recorded in a World Cup match
Norway's first World Cup quarter-final in the nation's history
Haaland's brace takes him to 7 tournament goals — level with Mbappé and Messi

yesterday.report: The stat sheet reads like a misprint: Brazil, the nation of jogo bonito, out-passed 581 to 291 in a knockout tie. Norway pressed high, moved the ball with total calm, and waited. On 79 minutes Haaland rose to head home a cross; in the 90th he collected the ball outside the box and arrowed a low drive past the goalkeeper. Brazil's 14 shots produced just four on target.
yesterday.report2: Neymar's stoppage-time penalty — his first goal of this World Cup — was no more than a farewell note. The five-time champions are out before the last eight, and a Norwegian side built on structure, running power and one unstoppable centre-forward marches on to Miami.

star.name: Erling Haaland
star.line: A header and a 25-yard low drive in eleven minutes. Seven goals in five games — and next up, England in Saturday's Miami quarter-final.

aside.name: Neymar, 34
aside.line: His stoppage-time penalty — Brazil's only goal — may well be his final act at a World Cup.

yesterday.whatItMeans: Norway meet England in Saturday's Miami quarter-final (23:00). Brazil go home earlier than at any World Cup in a generation.

events.text: Red card: Quansah (ENG), 2nd half — England finished the game with ten men

facts.text: Kick-off delayed an hour by lightning storms over Mexico City
England's 33% possession — their lowest at a World Cup since records began in 1966
49 England clearances, their most in a World Cup game since 1990

yesterday.report: An hour late after lightning storms, and worth every minute of the wait. Bellingham scored twice in the space of 90 seconds to silence 80,824 at the Azteca; Quiñones headed one back from a corner before the break. When Rangel brought down Gordon, Kane converted the 60th-minute penalty — then the match turned: Quansah saw red, VAR gave Mexico a penalty of their own, and Jiménez buried it.
yesterday.report2: The last twenty minutes were a siege. England made 49 clearances — their most at a World Cup since 1990 — and finished with 33% of the ball, their lowest on record. It didn't matter. Mexico's proud unbeaten home World Cup record ends on the ground where it was built, and England march on with what ESPN called the best away win in their history.

star.name: Jude Bellingham
star.line: Two goals in 90 seconds — the first man to score twice at the Azteca in a World Cup match since Diego Maradona in 1986.

aside.name: Harry Kane
aside.line: Ice-cold from the spot in front of a hostile wall of noise. Five tournament goals — two behind the leaders.

yesterday.whatItMeans: England face Haaland's Norway in Miami on Saturday night — a heavyweight quarter-final between the tournament's form sides.

today.preview: Neighbours, rivals, and two of the tournament's best attacks meet far from home. Spain have looked the more controlled side, patient and suffocating in possession; Portugal have been ruthless in transition, scoring in bursts. European champions against Iberian pride — knockout football rarely gifts a derby this big, this early.
watch: The midfield duel: Spain's control against Portugal's counter-punch
Winner faces the USA or Belgium in Friday's Los Angeles quarter-final

keyMan.name: Mikel Oyarzabal
keyMan.line: Four goals this tournament, quietly among the Golden Boot chasers — and Spain's most reliable big-game finisher.

today.preview: The co-hosts ride a wave of home support into one of America's loudest stadiums — with a boost from the committee room: FIFA reversed Folarin Balogun's red-card suspension on review, freeing the striker to lead the line. Belgium's post-golden-generation side is dangerous but beatable, and Seattle will believe.

keyMan.name: Folarin Balogun
keyMan.line: Suspension overturned, point to prove. The Seattle crowd will make him the story of the night if he scores.
